areas.name: South Pioneer Peak
areas.blurb: South Pioneer Peak is the trail-accessible southern summit of Pioneer Peak, the Chugach landmark standing over the Knik River valley south of Palmer. A relentless ridge trail climbs from near sea level to a saddle, and a rough scramble leads to the top.

routes.name: Pioneer Ridge
routes.rock_grade: Off-and-on Class 3 scrambling on the summit ridge
routes.best_season: Summer, once snow has melted off the saddle and ridge; patches can linger into late June.
routes.overview: The Pioneer Ridge route climbs about 6,000 feet in one push from the Knik River valley, through forest and brush onto open tundra ridge and then to a saddle near 5,200 ft. A rough, exposed scramble along the ridge reaches the south summit.
routes.beta: Follow the steep trail through forest and alder to treeline, then up tundra and switchbacks to the saddle near 5,200 ft. From there the route heads northeast along the ridge, rolling at first and steepening, with off-and-on Class 3 scrambling near the top. Keep to the east side of the ridge after the false summit.
routes.descent_text: Descend the same way, with extra care on the loose, exposed ridge, then the long trail back to the car.
hazards: Exposure and loose rock on the ridge
Sparse water above the lower trail
Heat and insects in the forest
Devil's club and thick brush on the lower trail

approach_logistics.trailhead: Pioneer Ridge Trailhead, Knik River Road
